title: Finite algebraic envelopes and the Boone–Higman conjecture

issues.description: The two load-bearing external inputs are cited, not proved: Zaremsky's type-(A) finite-presentation criterion for twisted Brin–Thompson groups (f.p. acting group, f.g. point stabilizers, finitely many orbits on 2-subsets, faithful action), and Krstić–McCool's theorem that St_n(R) is finitely presented for a finitely presented noncommutative ring R with n>=4. The paper states them in the form it uses, and that form matches what I recall of the sources, but I did not check them against the originals.
issues.evidence: Theorem zaremsky is quoted from [Zaremsky2024Finite, Thm A/Cor B] and [BelkZaremsky2022, Thm 3.4]; Prop affine uses [KrsticMcCool1999, Thm 3].

issues.location: compiler.tex, invariance under equations and contexts
issues.description: The equation-step invariance case analysis is terse. It covers slide, quota, entry, merge, internal, cleanup and q_ok->Z steps. I re-derived each case, including several q_ok sectors with different cell counts merging into one Z-cleanup trajectory, and all are consistent. The argument still depends on the reader rebuilding several implicit facts: Z-cleanup is forward-deterministic, internal components preserve bases and boundary flags, and anchor count bounds the payload.
issues.evidence: In Sec. A.4–A.5, the claims 'Cleanup equations give the same result by forward determinism' and 'Passing validation forces both α and ω' are each stated in one line.

coverage: Read the whole paper (introduction, reduction, affine, kernel, action, algebra, bootstrap, compiler appendix) and checked by hand: the HNN commutator identity and the effective Britton procedure; the cyclic-module lemma, including the d_{bc} identity in B⊗B^op; every step of the affine relative presentation (closure of the coefficient set, column independence via XY=ZYX, commutations, additivity, the conjugation formula, inverse homomorphisms); the transition endomorphism and injectivity of F. Kernel annihilation: the elementary-root conjugation formulas, the W-compression matrix H and its inverse, the corner conjugations, b=d+d*+1-E-F with b^2=1 and bEb=F, the exact D-conjugation in both the cross-pair and same-pair cases, the orthogonal-root commutation, the four-corner idempotents (idempotence, orthogonality, E00+E01=E0, d_v,d_v^* relations), and z=z^2. Action: the mapping torus with a non-injective endomorphism, the affine limit, faithfulness via b_* and strict stage nesting, two-transitivity through simplicity of A, point stabilizers, and the diagonal commutator embedding. Algebra: the partial-affine monoid composition formula, simplicity by selectors, i(h)=c_h-c_ζ, the contracted-algebra presentation, the tail corner q=e0-e1 with the Leavitt pair identities, commutation with φ(B), and the separator detector. Bootstrap: strict dependency m<n, stability, every critical-pair case (selectors at different and equal stages, code/selector, code/code including zero class), Newman's lemma, κ, c, and selector existence. Compiler: the quiver/sector structure, the validator indegree argument, the component lemma, grade accounting (including the merge, 4=4), and invariance for every equation type. Also used the sibling entries on the shared board.
main_claim: The Boone–Higman conjecture: a finitely generated group has decidable word problem iff it embeds in a finitely presented simple group. The proof goes through a finitely presented group Γ, the mapping torus of B^6⋊St_6(B⊗B^op) under the coefficient endomorphism φ, which acts faithfully and two-transitively on M_∞^6 with finitely generated point stabilizers. Zaremsky's criterion then embeds Γ in a finitely presented simple group.
